newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: SRI LANKA INDUSTRY SAYS POWER HIKE TO HIT EXPORTS.
newsitem.headline: SRI LANKA INDUSTRY SAYS POWER HIKE TO HIT EXPORTS.

text.p: Sri Lankan industry is to ask the government to reconsider a proposed hike in power tariffs that is likely to hit export-oriented firms, the independent Island newspaper said on Thursday.

The newspaper quoted the Sri Lanka National Chambers of Industry and Commerce (NCIC) as saying it would make representations to President Chandrika Kumaratunga over last week's announcement by Ceylon Electricity Board (CEB) that power rates would rise by an average 11.6 percent from September 1.
NCIC president Patrick Amarasinghe said a rise in power rates could be better absorbed by domestic industries as they could pass on the cost to consumers.
But exporters had to bear the cost themselves since in most cases purchase prices for exports were fixed in advance.
"Half-way through a deal we cannot increase the prices, so the industrialists (exporters) end up absorbing the cost," Amarasinghe was quoted as saying.
Garments make up most of Sri Lanka's industrial exports.
The CEB, announcing an across-the-board tariff increase, said it was necessary to raise money to bring in additional generation capacity to meet rising demand for power.
The previous tariff increase of eight percent was in January 1996.
